correctness.rationale: The exact scope is two successor predicates sampled from independent uniform linear orders and FO2 quantifier rank at most three. The factorial-moment count is derived directly from compatible directed paths, yielding independent Poisson(1) overlaps. The recursive unary FO2 rank-type construction and high-probability isolation of the four endpoints and overlap pairs show that rank-two vertex profiles depend only on zero/one/at-least-two overlap counts. Explicit rank-three formulas realize each nine-state cell. Transcendence of e gives fifty distinct values; rank-two yields twelve. The standalone checker enumerated all second orders through size seven and verified moments, type-profile invariance on 54 clean sampled instances, and distinct subset-sum polynomials. These finite checks support, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The natural two-independent-successor model is central to recent two-variable finite-model investigations. The theorem completely classifies its first nontrivial finite-rank random logical probability spectrum and proves a sharp strict increase from twelve rank-two to fifty rank-three limits. The precise invariant explains which adjacency coincidences are logically observable, rather than giving a routine isolated numerical probability. The fifty cases all arise from the full Boolean expressive fragment, not a contrived parameter slice.
